A CV is a list, and lists are good at one thing: order. Mine runs to seven pages and tells you what I did and when. It does not tell you that the survival models from my PhD turned up again in a churn project at PwC and then in a course I teach. Those three facts sit on three different pages.

I work with networks and knowledge graphs in my research, so reading my own career as a flat list had started to feel like a small hypocrisy. The [interactive version](/cv-network.html) is the fix.

## What it does

I sit at the centre with ten hubs around me: appointments, industry, education, publications, the research pipeline, teaching, methods, leadership, talks and honours. Click a hub and it opens into its own subgraph. Click again and you reach the actual CV text, with the DOI where there is one.

All 162 entries on one screen would be a hairball, which is the standard way network visualisations fail. Drill-down keeps about a dozen nodes in view at a time.

## The useful part

The dashed lines are the reason to build this at all. Select a paper and its co-authors, its method and the conference talk it came from appear from other parts of the graph. Select a method and you see every paper, project and course that uses it.

The co-author view was the one that taught me something. Draw a line between any two people who share a paper or a talk with me and the picture falls into five separate groups, with two people standing alone. I had never seen my collaborations as five conversations that do not talk to each other. A list of names cannot show that.

## How it is built

I built it in one evening with an AI coding assistant, and the design decisions are mine.

It is a single web page with no server behind it. The layout is a D3 force simulation, and the whole CV lives in one block of plain data at the top, one line per entry. Updating the CV means editing that block. The co-author lines are computed from the paper and talk links, so a new paper draws its own lines.

There are three reading lenses, for a hiring committee, a collaborator or a student, each bringing different hubs forward. There is also a plain list view, because some readers want a CV to behave like a CV, and because graphs are miserable on small phones.

## What I left out

My phone number, my referees' email addresses and my marks. A public page is public all the way down, including its source.

It does not replace the PDF. A screening committee wants a document it can print and tick. This is for everyone else.

*Statistically Yours, Aritra*
